_comment: REAL EVENT ROUTE - adapted from Gab's 'Amazing Race Barcelona (GAB LAB Edition)' script, transcribed in full at docs/BARCELONA-SCRIPT.md. This is the actual event, not test data - but several stops are SIMPLIFIED from the original script to fit what the app can automate today. Every simplification is called out in that checkpoint's own _note field below, and summarized in README.md. Review before game day - especially the multi-photo stops (4, 5), the Detour (9, originally a choice), the Roadblock/chocolate stops (6, 7 - AI can't verify these well, lean on host judgement), and the two cross-team bonuses from the original script that are NOT implemented anywhere in the app (best photo at stop 1, completion-order bonus at stop 4) - those need a host to award manually if you want to keep them.

checkpoints.name: Arc de Triomf
checkpoints.clue: Barcelona welcomed the world here in 1888. Your adventure begins beneath a red-brick gateway built for the occasion. Find it, and prepare to go FOURWARD.
checkpoints.instruction: Teams have 5 minutes to find random objects/poses and create your own "Barcelona coat of arms" - the whole team, using whatever you can find around you.
aiCriteria: the whole team together
posed creatively as a coat-of-arms / crest, using found objects or poses
checkpoints._note: SIMPLIFIED: original script gives the best photo across all four teams a 3-minute head start. That's a cross-team comparison the engine can't do (it only ever judges one team at a time) - a host has to eyeball all four submissions and decide. Not automated here.

checkpoints.name: The Mammoth, Parc de la Ciutadella
checkpoints.clue: A prehistoric giant is hiding nearby. He hasn't moved in over a century, but today he's waiting for you. Find Barcelona's stone mammoth.
checkpoints.instruction: Take a photograph of your entire team apparently running away from the mammoth.
aiCriteria: the stone mammoth statue clearly visible
the whole team in frame, posed as if fleeing/running from it
checkpoints._note: SIMPLIFIED: the original also asks for two more finds (something representing Catalonia, another animal, a fountain) and a stranger-filmed 15-second video. Only the mammoth photo is the automated gate here - ask about the rest informally if you want the full flavour.

checkpoints.name: Placa de Sant Jaume
checkpoints.clue: TWO GOVERNMENTS. ONE SQUARE. Leave the mammoth behind. Find the historic Barcelona square where the government of Catalonia faces the government of Barcelona.
checkpoints.instruction: Send a photo of your ENTIRE team in the square.
aiCriteria: the whole team together
an open square with grand government-building facades visible

checkpoints.name: Pont del Bisbe - Lost in Barcelona
checkpoints.clue: Find the bridge that looks centuries old...but isn't. Welcome to the Gothic Quarter. Your challenge is called LOST IN BARCELONA.
checkpoints.instruction: Photograph your whole team together under the famous bridge on Carrer del Bisbe, with a gargoyle or piece of Gothic stonework visible somewhere in the same shot, on a narrow medieval street.
aiCriteria: the whole team together
the ornate stone bridge over Carrer del Bisbe
Gothic-style carved stonework (a gargoyle or similar) visible
a narrow historic street
checkpoints._note: SIMPLIFIED: the original script asks for SIX separate photos (the bridge, a gargoyle, something Roman, a Catalan flag, a stranger, a narrow street) - combined here into one shot with the most iconic elements. Also drops the original's completion-order bonus (1st/2nd/3rd/4th team get 5/3/1/0-minute bonuses) - that needs live cross-team timing a host would track, not something the engine compares.

checkpoints.name: Roadblock - Parles Catala?
checkpoints.clue: WHO HAS THE GIFT OF THE GAB? Choose ONE teammate - once chosen, you cannot change.
checkpoints.instruction: That racer must find a stranger willing to teach them how to say in Catalan: "Hello, we're doing a race. Can you help us?" - plus one more Catalan expression of the stranger's choosing (no Google Translate). Then teach it to the rest of the team. Photograph the whole team together with the stranger who taught you.
aiCriteria: the whole team gathered together with an extra person (the stranger) who taught them
everyone looks engaged, not just posing
checkpoints._note: AI CANNOT VERIFY THIS: a photo can't confirm the team actually learned the Catalan phrase correctly - the original calls for a video of everyone saying it. The photo gate here only confirms they found and are with a willing stranger. Real verification is a live/host judgement call - ask the team to say the phrase to you.

checkpoints.name: Mercat de la Boqueria
checkpoints.clue: Enter Barcelona's most colourful market. Your mission is to find something RED, something you have NEVER eaten, and something costing less than 2 euros.
checkpoints.instruction: Photograph all three items together: something red, something none of you has ever eaten, and something under 2 euros.
aiCriteria: a red-coloured food item
an unusual or unfamiliar food item
all items shown together in one frame, market setting visible

checkpoints.name: Carrer de Petritxol - Chocolate Challenge
checkpoints.clue: Leave the market behind and find a tiny street with a very big sweet tooth. Chocolate has been tempting Barcelonans here for generations.
checkpoints.instruction: Buy one chocolate-related treat to share (keep the receipt). One teammate closes their eyes; a second may only use their VOICE to guide them; the blindfolded racer must feed a bite to a THIRD teammate, hands-free. Photograph the moment of feeding, with the treat and receipt visible.
aiCriteria: a chocolate treat and a receipt visible together
team members in a hands-free feeding pose or the moment right after
checkpoints._note: AI CANNOT FULLY VERIFY THIS: the original wants a video of the actual blindfolded feeding to confirm no hands were used. A single photo is a weaker check - lean on host judgement or ask the team to describe what happened if the photo is ambiguous.

checkpoints.name: Temple of Augustus - BARCINO
checkpoints.clue: Long before Barcelona had this name, four columns stood above the Roman city. Find them and discover what Barcelona was called then.
checkpoints.instruction: Find the four ancient Roman columns, then answer: what was Roman Barcelona called? (one word)
checkpoints._note: Matches the script's own rule exactly: wrong answers get a 2-minute penalty ("no response for 2 minutes").

checkpoints.name: Detour - Brains
checkpoints.clue: DETOUR: BRAINS OR BALLS. You must survive the elegant Barcelona before entering El Raval.
checkpoints.instruction: What mountain overlooks Barcelona from the southwest? (one word)
checkpoints._note: SIMPLIFIED: the original Detour is a real CHOICE between Brains (5 trivia questions) and Balls (30 consecutive football touches as a team, on video) - the app has no branching-choice mechanic, so this is fixed to one Brains question. If a team would rather physically do the football challenge, have the host verify it in person and call manualUnlock() for them instead of using this checkpoint.

checkpoints.name: Botero's Cat, Rambla del Raval
checkpoints.clue: Cross Barcelona's most famous boulevard. Somewhere in Raval waits an enormous animal. It doesn't roar. It doesn't bite. And despite its size...it's a cat.
checkpoints.instruction: Your entire team must recreate the pose of the giant bronze cat using your bodies. You may NOT take the photo yourselves - find a stranger to take it for you.
aiCriteria: the bronze cat statue visible
the whole team posed imitating the cat's pose

checkpoints.name: Secret Mission
checkpoints.clue: You've completed your journey through Barcelona. Almost. There is one more task before the finish.
checkpoints.instruction: Complete your team's secret mission (see your teammates for details) and photograph the proof.
aiCriteria: the whole team visibly involved in the moment described
checkpoints._note: Radius widened to 150m - the original script gives an approximate area ("≈41.3785, 2.1691"), not one exact spot, since this mission happens wherever the team finds a willing stranger nearby.

red.instruction: Find a stranger willing to teach your entire team a dance move. Photograph the whole team performing it together with the stranger.
aiCriteria: the whole team plus a stranger
everyone mid-dance-move together

blue.instruction: Convince THREE strangers to join your team and shout "VISCA BARCELONA!" simultaneously. Photograph the moment.
aiCriteria: the team plus three additional people (strangers)
everyone appears to be shouting/celebrating together

green.instruction: Find people from THREE different countries. Photograph your team with all three together.
aiCriteria: the whole team
at least two additional people who appear to be from elsewhere, posed together with the team

yellow.instruction: Find a stranger and ask them to invent a new, ridiculous name for your team. Photograph the whole team with that stranger.
aiCriteria: the whole team plus one extra person (the stranger)
a fun, celebratory pose

checkpoints.name: Barcelo Raval - Final Memory Challenge
checkpoints.clue: You've crossed Barcelona. Now rise above it. Find the circular rooftop overlooking El Raval. Your race ends at the top. DO NOT RUN INSIDE THE HOTEL.
checkpoints.instruction: Reaching the rooftop does not mean you've won. Arrange these six stops in the exact order you visited them, as their codes separated by commas with no spaces: ARC (Arc de Triomf), MAMMOTH (the stone mammoth), JAUME (Placa de Sant Jaume), PETRITXOL (the chocolate street), AUGUSTUS (the Roman columns / BARCINO), CAT (Botero's cat). Example format: mammoth,arc,cat,jaume,augustus,petritxol
checkpoints._note: Wrong-answer penalty set to match the script's own rule: "wait 60 seconds before attempting again." Once correct, the closing-ceremony speech (1st/2nd/3rd/4th, from the original PDF) is for the host to read aloud on the rooftop - the leaderboard already has the real finishing order and times, the app doesn't need to say it.
